cases.note: GNU: `echo hi > /dev/full; echo $?; echo next` in debian:stable-slim prints bash's `bash: line 1: echo: write error: No space left on device`, then 1 and next. Mirage keeps its redirect voice (workspace/executor/redirect.py); the exit status and the line going on match GNU. A refused `>` of output written at once (printf, echo) creates no file and leaves an existing one as it was, where GNU truncates and creates at open; a streaming command keeps what landed (capacity_a_refused_stream_keeps_what_landed).
cases.command: printf 12345678 > /data2/a; echo $?; printf 123 > /data2/b; echo $?; test -e /data2/b; echo $?; echo next

cases.note: GNU cp words a failed write after the open as `cp: error writing '...'`; mirage's cp reports `cannot create regular file` for any write failure, a divergence that predates capacity.

expect.stderr: cp: cannot create regular file '/data2/c': Disk quota exceeded

cases.note: A move into a capped mount copies first, so a refused copy keeps the source; mirage leaves an empty destination, where GNU mv keeps the bytes that fit. GNU words the failed write as `mv: error writing '...'`; mirage's mv says `cannot create regular file`, as its cp does.

expect.stderr: mv: cannot create regular file '/data2/big': Disk quota exceeded

cases.command: printf 12345678 > /data2/a; echo $?; printf 123 > /data2/b; echo $?; echo next

cases.note: 1K blocks, each figure rounded up as GNU df rounds: 1000 bytes used reads 1, the 1047576 bytes left read 1024.
GNU sed exits 4 when it cannot write the edit (`couldn't write ... items`); mirage words it as its other refused edit write, `couldn't edit`, and exits 4.

expect.stderr: sed: couldn't edit /data2/s: Disk quota exceeded

cases.note: GNU sed exits 4 when a w file cannot be written (`couldn't write ... items`); mirage reports the w file in its open-file voice and exits 4.

expect.stderr: sed: couldn't open file /data2/out: Disk quota exceeded

cases.note: The seeded /data holds far more than 1 byte: the load keeps it, a read and a removal pass, and only growth is refused.
cases.command: cat /data/a.txt > /dev/null; echo $?; rm /data/a.txt; echo $?; printf x > /data/new; echo $?
